objective: The live database follows the Kaggle dataset with no manual step. A daily EventBridge rule runs a new SportsDataRefresh function (outside the VPC) that downloads Games.csv, PlayerStatistics.csv, TeamStatistics.csv, Players.csv and the current season's LeagueSchedule file singly through kagglehub into SportsDataBucket under nba-eoin/, then asynchronously invokes the existing SportsDataLoad for the current season. A game whose stored score or teams disagree with the dataset is skipped, reported and alarmed, never applied, and no longer aborts the load.
acceptance_criteria: Test-first: commit the failing tests alone before any implementation. The tests use a fake DatasetSource and moto, never the network and never a real token.

Add app.events.kaggle_source: a DatasetSource Protocol (fetch one named file of the dataset into a directory and return its path; a file the dataset does not have raises DatasetFileNotFound) and KagglehubSource, the only code importing kagglehub. KagglehubSource downloads one file per call with kagglehub.dataset_download('eoinamoore/historical-nba-data-and-player-box-scores', path=<name>), never the whole dataset and never into a DataFrame, with KAGGLEHUB_CACHE set to a directory under the function's /tmp. Tests cover the fake, and the call shape with kagglehub itself faked.

Token handling: app.events.refresh_handler reads the token with Secrets Manager GetSecretValue on the secret named by KAGGLE_SECRET_ARN at invocation time, then sets os.environ['KAGGLE_API_TOKEN'] in-process and removes KAGGLE_USERNAME and KAGGLE_KEY from the environment (kagglehub's lookup order is undocumented, so only the token variable is left). The token is never in the Lambda's configuration, never logged, never in an exception message, never written to disk by this code; every failure is re-raised from None with the token redacted. A test asserts the token value appears in no log line, no raised message and no returned value, including when the fake source raises an error containing it.

Refresh order: validate config (SPORTS_DATA_BUCKET, KAGGLE_SECRET_ARN, LOAD_FUNCTION_NAME; an unset one fails before any AWS call) -> read secret -> for each of Games.csv, PlayerStatistics.csv, TeamStatistics.csv, Players.csv: fetch, check, upload to s3://<bucket>/nba-eoin/<name>, delete the local copy before the next (peak /tmp is one file; ephemeral storage is 2048 MB because kagglehub may leave a server-side zip beside the extracted file) -> fetch and check the current season's LeagueSchedule<YY>_<YY>.csv (DatasetFileNotFound is skipped and logged, any other error fails) -> invoke SportsDataLoad with InvocationType Event and payload exactly {"seasons": [<current season>]}. The load is invoked only after every required file is in the bucket; any earlier failure raises and invokes nothing.

Never overwrite a good copy with a bad one (the bucket is not versioned). Before uploading a file require it non-empty, its header line equal to the first line of the object already in the bucket when there is one, and its size not below that object's size. s3:ListBucket with a prefix condition is what lets a missing object (404) be told from a denied one. With no object in the bucket there is no baseline: the header must contain the column names the loader requires. A failed check raises DatasetRefreshRejected naming the file and both sizes, uploads nothing further and invokes nothing. Tests: empty file, wrong header, shrunk file, first-ever upload, and that the existing object is untouched after a rejection.

The current season is derived from the invocation date in America/Toronto: from 1 October a date belongs to season YYYY-(YY+1), an earlier date to the season that began the previous October. A scheduled event ({} or an EventBridge scheduled event) uses it; an event {"seasons": [...]} is validated by nba_history.validate_seasons and used instead, so a manual run can still name any seasons and fetch their schedule files. Any other event shape raises InvalidRefreshEvent before any AWS call. Tests pin the boundaries (30 Sep, 1 Oct, 31 Dec, 1 Jan, 1 Jul) with a frozen clock.

A season with a schedule file but no games yet (1 October to the first game) loads without error and stores its schedule rows; a test proves it. A mixed dataset version (Kaggle updating between the four per-file downloads) is accepted: the loader already stores a game without a box score and fills it on a later run, and a test with Games.csv ahead of PlayerStatistics.csv shows the second run completing it.

Change the loader so a stored game whose teams or final score disagree with the dataset is not a DatasetError: that game is left exactly as stored, counted and named in a new SeasonReport.games_conflicting (game id, stored score, dataset score, both team pairs), every other game and the schedule load in the same transaction, and the report line names the conflicts. Malformed data, unknown teams and every other DatasetError stay fatal. app.events.load_handler returns the conflicts in its result, logs one warning line per conflict and emits a CloudWatch EMF metric GamesConflicting (namespace Fanwire/SportsData, value = the run's conflicts, 0 when none) through aws_lambda_powertools Metrics. Tests that expected DatasetError for a disagreeing score or teams change in the tests commit, named in its message. nba_history.py's docstring and 0x02b are corrected so none still says a corrected score aborts the load.
The kagglehub>=1.0.3 runtime dependency is added by the Director PR that merges this spec. The unit must not touch backend/pyproject.toml. pip-audit and the image build stay green with it.

Infra, Fanwire-Data: a secretsmanager.Secret 'KaggleApiToken', secretName fanwire/kaggle-api-token, encrypted with the Data CMK, RemovalPolicy RETAIN, with a generated placeholder value (the human overwrites it with put-secret-value; the placeholder makes a first run before that fail loud, which is intended), exposed to App the way the other Data secrets are. Its description says it holds the Kaggle API token and is set by hand.

Infra, Fanwire-App: backendFunction gains an option to run outside the VPC (no vpc, subnets or security group, and no VpcNetworkInterfaces statement for that function). Every existing function's template is unchanged, proven by a before/after synth diff in the PR body. New function SportsDataRefresh: the shared image, command app.events.refresh_handler.handler, 10 min timeout, 1024 MB, 2048 MB ephemeral storage, outside the VPC (it needs Kaggle and AWS APIs, never the database, and avoids the NAT), environment SPORTS_DATA_BUCKET, KAGGLE_SECRET_ARN and LOAD_FUNCTION_NAME only (no DATABASE_URL, no token). Its statements, none with a wildcard resource beyond the existing nba-eoin/* object prefix: secretsmanager:GetSecretValue on the exact secret ARN; s3:GetObject and s3:PutObject on arnForObjects('nba-eoin/*'); s3:ListBucket on the bucket with an s3:prefix condition of nba-eoin/*; kms:GenerateDataKey on the CMK; lambda:InvokeFunction on SportsDataLoad's exact ARN. infra/test/iam-policy.test.ts passes with no loosening.

Infra: an events.Rule 'SportsDataRefreshSchedule', cron(0 9 * * ? *) (09:00 UTC, after the dataset's nightly upload), one target, retryAttempts 0, the AccountDeletionSchedule pattern. SportsDataLoad gains an EventInvokeConfig with retryAttempts 0 (an async invoke must not retry a failed or locked load; the advisory lock and the next day's run cover it). The two tests in app-stack.test.ts that say nothing invokes SportsDataLoad and that there are no EventInvokeConfigs change deliberately: SportsDataRefresh's role is the only invoker of SportsDataLoad, the refresh schedule is the only rule, and Migration still has none.

Infra alarms: the derived alarm loop gives SportsDataRefresh an Errors and a Throttles alarm, and SportsDataLoad keeps its own, so a failed download and a failed load both alarm into the existing topic. Add one alarm, SportsDataConflictsAlarm, on the Fanwire/SportsData GamesConflicting metric, Maximum > 0 over one period, same topic, missing data not breaching. infra/test/alarms.test.ts's pinned count rises by exactly 3 from the value on main when the unit starts, with its comment naming the three; every other alarm is unchanged.

infra/iam/** is unchanged and CloudFormation's execution role needs no new version: every cfn-exec-policy, iam-policy and permissions-boundary test passes in every domain mode. If synth proves a ceiling is missing, stop and report it to the Director; do not widen anything. Nobody runs cdk deploy.
The unit touches no live database, no AWS account, no Kaggle and no token. No Alembic revision is added; a migration here is a defect.

Docs, same pass: wiki/CodeContext/Modules/0x02b-events-loading.md states the refresh flow (schedule, function, files, the shrink and header guard, the current-season rule, conflict handling and metric, the secret, the alarms); 0x02-events.md's resolved decisions follow; 0x00a-architecture-infra.md lists the function, rule, secret and alarm count; 0x00-architecture.md's tables follow. The manual path stays documented as the fallback. Standards/build-deployment-post-deploy.md, TODO/**, Prompts/** and the backlog are Director follow-up PRs, not written here.

The Director reruns: docker compose -p fanwire run --rm backend-test; npm run build, npm run lint, npm test and npm run synth in infra/; ruff and mypy in backend/. The PR body carries the synth diff of every stack (only the resources above added; no existing resource changed apart from SportsDataLoad's EventInvokeConfig), the human's first-run checklist, and the mixed-version and July-September schedule limits stated plainly.
